items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: So he asked me to get a drummer and I got Leroy Williams, another home drummer.

ctx.x: About 2:00 in the morning, he and the drummer, a

friend of mine from Chicago, Leroy Williams, had settled in New York, and he was looking for me. I'm walking down the street -- I had just left Billy Greene's brother's house, little Donald Greene, and I'm on my way home. It was about 2:00 in the morning. This car pulls right up on the sidewalk and blocked my path. So I'm wondering what's going on. Two guys jumped out and it's Leroy and Archie Shepp. Archie say, "Man, you going up to Newport. Play tomorrow afternoon." I say, "Wait a minute, man. I can't play your…

But I said, "Okay, I'll go." He didn't really have to twist my arm too much. I wanted to see what Newport was like. I hadn't been up there since the riot. Anyway, we took off that night. We got to Newport the next afternoon and they had us sandwiched in. He had Howard Johnson on tuba. He had Grachan Moncur on trombone, himself on tenor, and he had a poet, crazy guy, Leon Bibbs (PHONETIC) -- not Leon Bibbs, but --
